# Usable and rejected scans by age Breasts are averaged within each age band, separately for NORMAL, BENIGN and CANCER, twice: once using only the scans that pass the test (usable), and once using only the scans it rejects. In each, a breast is the mean of the scans used. This shows what the kept and the discarded scans look like at different ages. ::: {#cell-fig-usable-by-age .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} plot_bands(summaries["usable"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![**Usable scans.** Mean prepared curve of NORMAL, BENIGN and CANCER breasts, one panel per age band (each breast is the mean of its usable scans), with ±1 SD across breasts shaded. The dashed line is the usable-scan water threshold over q 20–22.](normal_by_age_files/figure-html/fig-usable-by-age-output-1.png){#fig-usable-by-age width=767 height=293} ::: ::: ::: {#cell-fig-rejected-by-age .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} plot_bands(summaries["rejected"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![**Rejected scans.** As @fig-usable-by-age, but each breast is the mean of the scans the test rejects.](normal_by_age_files/figure-html/fig-rejected-by-age-output-1.png){#fig-rejected-by-age width=767 height=293} ::: ::: Mean water peak height (q 20–22) of each band's mean curve, with the number of breasts in brackets:

Breasts without an age are left out, and both figures share one y axis. The rejected scans look the same at every age and in every cohort, with a water peak near 0.2: once the water-bearing scans are taken out, what is left is fat, whatever the patient's age or label. The usable scans fall only a little with age, and CANCER stays about level while NORMAL and BENIGN drop, so in the older bands CANCER is the wettest. Only 2 CANCER breasts are under 40, so those curves say little.
